S86.01.needs: a signed-in account (removing a method may need re-confirmation)
S86.01.note: The sign-in methods list is rendered from SecuritySection, but the panel has no visible heading of its own in the code; the 'Passkeys and security keys' list is inside Advanced Account Security.
steps: Open Settings, then click Security in the left list.
Find the sign-in methods list: Email address, Password, Passkeys, and any Single sign-on or Linked account rows.
Click Change or Add on the Password row, and use Connect or Disconnect on a linked account row.
Look at whether every sign-in method is listed and whether you can add or remove one, and compare with Expected.
S86.01.where: Settings > Security, then the sign-in methods list (Email address, Password, Passkeys, Single sign-on, linked accounts)

S86.02.needs: a password account and access to its email for the reset step
S86.02.note: The Forgot password? link is on the sign-in page, not in Settings; the code does not show whether the password change asks for a recent re-authentication, only the current password.
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the Change Password section.
Type the Current Password, then a new password in New Password and Confirm Password.
Click Change Password and read the result line.
To test reset, sign out, go to the sign-in page, type your email, and click Forgot password?. Compare with Expected.
S86.02.where: Settings > Security > Change Password (current password, new password, confirm); reset a forgotten one from the sign-in page with Forgot password?

S86.03.needs: a browser with passkey support and a device that can create one
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the passkeys list.
Click Add a passkey and follow the browser prompt.
Click Rename on the new passkey, type a new name, and press Enter.
Click Remove passkey on a passkey you added, read the confirmation, and compare the list with Expected.
S86.03.where: Settings > Security > Passkeys section: Add a passkey, then Rename and Remove passkey on each row

labels.text: Scan this in your authenticator app

S86.04.needs: an authenticator app on a phone
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the two-factor section.
Click Enable two-factor and scan Scan this in your authenticator app with an authenticator app.
Type the current 6-digit code and confirm; read Two-factor authentication is now enabled on your account.
Sign out and sign in again: a code should be asked. Then click Turn off two-factor, confirm, and compare with Expected.
S86.04.where: Settings > Security > Enable two-factor; turn it off with Turn off two-factor

S86.05.note: The code shows a Print action only when a printer is available; the Print unavailable state also exists.
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and turn on two-factor first if it is off.
Look at the Backup codes list under Save your backup codes.
Click Download codes and check the file, or use Print if it is shown.
Click Replace backup codes, confirm, and check that the old codes are described as no longer working. Compare with Expected.
S86.05.where: Settings > Security > Save your backup codes (view), Download codes (download), Replace backup codes (regenerate)

S86.06.needs: a second browser or device signed in to the same account
steps: Open Settings and click Account.
Scroll to the Active sessions heading.
Read the Device, Location, Created and Last active columns for each row.
Sign in from a second browser and check that its row appears. Compare with Expected.
S86.06.where: Settings > Account > Active sessions (columns Device, Location, Created, Last active)

S86.07.needs: a linked device (CLI, VS Code, Chrome extension or desktop app)
S86.07.note: No list of devices that skip checks is shown; the Device sign-in toggle only sets approval by device code, and the earlier check said trusted-device lists are unavailable.
steps: Open Settings, click Account, and find the Linked devices section.
Read each linked device row: its kind, status and Personal sign-in or Workspace sign-in label.
Click Unlink device on a test device, read the confirmation, and confirm.
Open Security and look at the Device sign-in toggle. Compare the list and toggle with Expected.
S86.07.where: Settings > Account > Linked devices (remove link with Unlink device); Settings > Security > Device sign-in (toggle)

S86.08.needs: a phone or desktop app paired to the account
steps: Open Settings, click Account, and find Linked devices.
Read the kind label on each row: Desktop app, Mobile app, Chrome extension or Remote Control.
Click Unlink device on a test row, read the message, and confirm.
Compare the list with Expected.
S86.08.where: Settings > Account > Linked devices (rows for Desktop app, VS Code extension, Chrome extension, Mobile app, Remote Control); Unlink device

S86.09.note: The code shows no separate sign-out control for the device in the settings menu; this is the only in-settings path found for the current session.
steps: Open Settings, click Account, and find Active sessions.
Find the row for this browser and click Log out current session.
Read the dialog Log out this session? and click Log out.
Check that you return to the sign-in page. Compare with Expected.
S86.09.where: Settings > Account > Active sessions > the row marked as the current session > Log out current session

S86.10.needs: a second browser signed in to the same account
steps: Open Settings and click Security.
Scroll to the Log out of all devices row and click Log out.
Read the dialog Log out of all devices? and click Log out everywhere.
Check that you are returned to the sign-in page, then sign in from a second browser to see its session gone. Compare with Expected.
S86.10.where: Settings > Security > Log out of all devices > Log out

S86.11.needs: an email inbox for the test account
steps: Open Settings and click Notifications.
Find the Security alerts heading and read its description: sign-in, password, email, two-factor and device changes.
Turn the Security alerts control on or off and check the setting is saved.
Make a sign-in or password change from another device and check for an email. Compare with Expected.

S86.12.note: Some connectors disconnect through their own flow, for example GitHub uses its App installations.
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Open a connector that is connected.
Read its account details and find the Disconnect button.
Click Disconnect, read the confirmation, and compare with Expected.
S86.12.where: Settings > Connectors, open a connected connector, then Disconnect

steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Open a connected connector.
Find the Permissions granted box with the scopes list.
Read each scope sentence and its access badge, and compare with Expected.
S86.13.where: Settings > Connectors > open a connected connector > Permissions granted

S86.14.note: The UI calls revoking a key Delete Key, and the code does not show a masked key value; this was not confirmed in code.
steps: Open Settings, click Account, and click the API keys row.
Click Generate New API Key, enter a Key Name, and copy the key once shown.
Read the list: each key row should show its name, scopes and expiry, and the key itself should be masked.
Click Delete Key on the test key, read the warning, and confirm. Compare with Expected.
S86.14.where: Settings > Account > API keys > API Keys panel (Generate New API Key; Delete Key)

S86.23.note: The phrase Saved approvals appears only in the VS Code extension locale (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json), not in the web app.
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Open a connected connector and click Tool Permissions.
Look at each tool's current level, and change one to Always run without asking or Never run this tool.
Click Reset all to default and confirm the reset. Compare with Expected.
S86.23.where: Settings > Connectors > open a connector > Tool Permissions (Always run without asking, Needs approval each time, Never run this tool; Reset all to default)

S86.24.needs: a signed-in account (Skip approvals is blocked when the workspace does not allow it)
S86.24.note: The option labels are Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking and Skip approvals, not the names in Expected; enforcement is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts.
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities.
Find Default approval for tool actions and pick Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking, or Skip approvals.
Read the Saved and Synced to your account status after each change.
Start a chat that runs a tool and check whether it asks. Compare with Expected.
S86.24.where: Settings > Capabilities > Default approval for tool actions

S86.26.needs: a passkey or security key, and access to the account email
S86.26.note: The hardened mode is the Advanced Account Security card, and the support article and recovery files are not UI.
steps: Open Settings, click Security, and find the Advanced Account Security card.
Read its description: for accounts at higher risk, sign-in needs a passkey or security key.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security after entering the code from the email, and read the result.
Check that password and email-code sign-in stop working, then click Turn off Advanced Account Security to undo it if the test allows. Compare with Expected.
S86.26.where: Settings > Security > Advanced Account Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security
